title: Toward a Universal Characterization of Sudoku Puzzle Difficulty
abstract: arXiv:2507.21137v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In this paper we try to answer the question "What constitutes Sudoku difficulty rating across different Sudoku websites?" Using two distinct methods that can both solve every Sudoku puzzle, I propose two new metrics to characterize Sudoku difficulty. The first method is based on converting a Sudoku puzzle into its corresponding Satisfiability (SAT) problem. The first proposed metric is derived from SAT Clause Length Distribution which captures the structural complexity of a Sudoku puzzle including the number of given digits and the cells they are in. The second method simulates human Sudoku solvers by intertwining four popular Sudoku strategies within a backtracking algorithm called Nishio. The second metric is computed by counting the number of times Sudoku strategies are applied within the backtracking iterations of a randomized Nishio. translated_title: 迈向数独谜题难度的普适性刻画
translated_abstract: 在本文中，我们试图回答这样一个问题：“不同数独网站的数独难度评级究竟由什么构成？”我使用两种都能够求解所有数独谜题的不同方法，提出了两个刻画数独难度的新指标。第一种方法基于将数独谜题转换为其对应的可满足性（SAT）问题，第一个提出的指标源自SAT子句长度分布，它捕捉了数独谜题的结构复杂性，包括给定数字的数量及其所在位置。第二种方法通过在一种名为Nishio的回溯算法中交织四种流行的数独解题策略来模拟人类数独求解者，第二个指标则通过统计随机化Nishio回溯迭代中数独策略被应用的次数来计算。利用这两个指标，我分析了来自五个热门网站的超过一千个数独谜题。
tldr: 本文提出两个新指标——基于SAT子句长度分布的结构复杂度指标和基于随机化Nishio回溯算法中策略应用次数的模拟人类求解指标——用以普适地刻画不同数独网站的谜题难度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes two novel metrics—one derived from SAT clause length distribution and another from counting strategy applications in a randomized Nishio backtracking algorithm—to provide a universal characterization of Sudoku puzzle difficulty across different websites.
